source.title: Solution space and storage capacity of fully connected two-layer neural networks with generic activation functions

record.tranche_reason: Trains fully connected two-layer networks on random binary datasets and reports where training succeeds or stalls, extending the training-capacity question to a synthetic setting.
record.gate_note: The paper says it computed accuracy, but the reported results describe loss and estimated experimental storage capacity; no training classification-error values are given. The plotted loss values are figure-only. Replica predictions and cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures storage capacity and final hinge loss in two-layer fully connected classifiers on synthetic random data. V1 specifies convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100 and training classification error. V2 specifies teacher-student problems and extra student neurons; neither is tested here. No initialization, depth, learning-rate stability, or normalization comparison tests V3–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the experimental conclusion: attained capacity is below the replica-based 1-RSB estimate, and erf's experimental capacity exceeds ReLU's. The authors attribute the gap to nonconvexity and trapping in local minima, but do not directly establish that mechanism. Their broader theoretical conclusions concern finite infinite-width storage capacity, negative weight correlations, and activation-dependent symmetry breaking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient descent with Adam and hinge loss on random binary datasets in fully connected two-layer networks; the initialization is not stated. It does not use the cited CIFAR convolutional benchmark recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: For erf, loss behavior varies across N/K; the authors identify N/K = 50 as closest to the replica-analysis setting.

fits_no_version.finding: With NK = 10000 and Adam, estimated experimental storage capacity is about 2.5 for ReLU across tested N/K ratios and about 3.8 for erf at N/K = 50; erf outcomes vary across other ratios.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Algorithmically attained storage capacity in two-layer fully connected classifiers on random binary datasets depends on activation and input-to-hidden dimension ratio.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan
record.problems: The experiments use synthetic random datasets and two-layer fully connected networks, not the benchmark convolutional models in V1. Results are averaged over 10 datasets, but uncertainty estimates are not stated. Accuracy was computed but no accuracy outcomes are reported; training success is described through hinge loss and estimated storage capacity. Several result values are figure-only.

untested.parts: All: convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, training classification error, random initialization, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
All: realizable ReLU teacher-student problems, frequencies of spurious minima, and adding one or two student neurons.
All: depth degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks, or Fixup.
All: initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
All: squared-loss training across learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, recovery, and divergence.
All: normalization comparisons, accuracy gain per training time, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Failure to attain theoretical capacity in this different architecture and task does not limit V1. The teacher-student discussion and proposed negatively correlated initialization offer no direct tests of V2 or V4.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 benchmarks, convolutional architectures, SGD, corrupted labels specifically, and comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.

rows.subject: FCM with ReLU activations
rows.stage_stated: trained from randomly generated datasets; initialization not stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained with gradient descent using Adam and hinge loss with κ = 0; stopped below loss 10−5 or after 5000 epochs; results averaged over 10 datasets per combination.
rows.measure: Loss at end of training; authors estimate experimental storage capacity from the increase in loss.
rows.value: Experimental storage capacity estimated around α = 2.5; loss increases abruptly around α ≈ 2.5 across N/K values. Exact plotted loss values are figure only.
rows.note: Authors attribute the gap from theoretical capacity to gradient descent becoming trapped in local minima at large α. The measured outcome is loss, not reported classification error.
rows.check: The reported capacity estimate near α = 2.5 is accurate, but it does not measure V1's convolutional CIFAR classification-error outcome. A rise in zero-margin hinge loss does not establish substantial classification error. The proposed local-minimum explanation is conjectural.

rows.subject: FCM with erf activation
rows.stage_stated: trained from randomly generated datasets; initialization not stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained with gradient descent using Adam and hinge loss with κ = 0; stopped below loss 10−5 or after 5000 epochs; results averaged over 10 datasets per combination.
rows.measure: Loss at end of training; authors estimate experimental storage capacity from the loss results.
rows.value: Experimental storage capacity estimated around 3.8; exact plotted loss values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors identify N/K = 50 as closest to the replica-analysis setting. The result concerns loss and estimated capacity, not reported classification error.
rows.check: The text confirms the capacity estimate near 3.8 at N/K = 50. This fully connected synthetic-data experiment does not measure V1; classification-error outcomes are not reported.

rows.subject: FCM with erf activation
rows.stage_stated: trained from randomly generated datasets; initialization not stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained with gradient descent using Adam and hinge loss with κ = 0; stopped below loss 10−5 or after 5000 epochs; results averaged over 10 datasets per combination.
rows.value: Loss does not behave consistently across different N/K; exact plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The text gives no specific training-error or loss outcome for each ratio.
rows.check: This records a qualitative comparison across ratios, without individual numerical outcomes. It does not measure any listed version, and inconsistency across ratios cannot establish partial or absent classification-error recovery.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
